records.text: Pete Hegseth said that U.S. Central Command would hit Iran hard that night because Iran still had a chance to make a deal.
records.speaker: Pete Hegseth

appearances.snippet: But of course, he is busy because CENTCOM, Central Command, will be busy tonight because President Trump said we will be hitting Iran hard and we will be because Iran has a chance. To make a good deal, a great deal, to codify what they said they've been willing to do and they haven't been willing to do it.

verification.notes: A contemporaneous video transcript of Hegseths June 11, 2026 remarks at CENTCOM records him saying the command would be busy that night, that the United States would hit Iran hard, and that Iran still had a chance to make a negotiated deal.

sources.relevance: Contemporaneous video and transcript contain the quoted remarks.

records.text: Pete Hegseth said that Operation Epic Fury and the blockade had created a chance to secure an agreement under which Iran would never have a nuclear weapon.
records.speaker: Pete Hegseth

appearances.snippet: And Admiral Cooper and the team here at CENTCOM have done a phenomenal job from the beginning on Epic Fury and through this blockade, ensuring that we have a chance to reach that end state, which is: Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, which they say they don't want.

verification.notes: The contemporaneous video transcript records Hegseth crediting Operation Epic Fury and the blockade with creating a chance to reach an end state in which Iran would never have a nuclear weapon.

records.text: Asked about a U.S. capture-kill operation against Miguel Díaz-Canel in Cuba, Pete Hegseth said the military had options all over the map and that all options were on the table.
records.speaker: Pete Hegseth

appearances.snippet: How long would a U.S. military operation take to remove the communist regime in Cuba? And uh what would happen per se and how long would it take to, you know, re-establish order if President Trump (Donald J. Trump) were to decide to do a capture-kill operation with Miguel Diaz-Canel like he did with Maduro in ... we've got we've got options all over the map Just like we've got lots of options in CENTCOM why we're what that's that's our job Our building literally plans for a living so besides the Pentagon no one plans better than United States Central Command So to kind of bring it back home to while we're here those options are all all those options are on the table

verification.notes: The CENTCOM press exchange records a reporter asking about a capture-kill operation against Miguel Diaz-Canel. Hegseth answered that the military presents options at different scales, said options were all over the map, and concluded that those options were on the table.

records.text: Owens said CNN reported that a U.S. Central Command intelligence officer emailed military analysts seeking creative and unconventional ideas to pressure, capture, and punish Iran.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But CNN came out today with just an incredible headline that the U.S. military is now asking troops for creative and unconventional ideas to punish Iran. ... An officer in the U.S. Central Command's intelligence branch, if we're still calling it intelligence, wrote in a message that was sent on Wednesday to a broad group of military analysts, according to a source that was familiar with the message.

verification.notes: CNN's own transcript and report describe a Central Command intelligence-branch email sent to a broad group of military analysts seeking creative and unconventional ways to pressure and punish Iran. The statement accurately represents CNN's report.
